analysis_title: KV-Cache Timing Attack: Leakage vs Overhead Pareto Curve (Week 13)

pareto_points.label: Full APC disable
pareto_points.note: Destroys oracle completely. +640.5% TTFT overhead — unacceptable for production latency SLAs.

pareto_points.label: CacheSolidarity / PrefixWall (Paper 8)
pareto_points.note: Retains 70% same-tenant cache reuse. Cross-tenant hits are masked at miss_ttft (oracle destroyed). 32 bytes metadata overhead per cached block.

pareto_points.label: Presidio-gated selective isolation (novel, Week 13)
pareto_points.note: Presidio NER + condition regex flags ~30% of prompts as PII-bearing. Only those prompts are cache-isolated; the remaining 70% benefit from full prefix-cache reuse. Pareto-dominates M1 at same leakage level but significantly lower TTFT overhead.

improvement_table.caption: Table 3: Leakage-vs-overhead Pareto curve. M3 (novel) achieves the same oracle destruction as M1 at 71.3% lower relative TTFT overhead by isolating only PII-bearing prompts.
improvement_table.m3_vs_m1_note: M3 overhead: +178.0%  vs  M1 overhead: +619.3%. M3 saves 71.3% relative overhead while achieving identical leak reduction.

arxiv_section5_summary.narrative: We evaluate four points on the leakage-vs-overhead Pareto frontier (Table 3). The unprotected baseline (M0) has TTFT = 90.2 ms and SR = 1.0. Full APC disable (M1) destroys the timing oracle (SR = 0.0005) but incurs +619.3% TTFT overhead, which violates production latency SLAs. CacheSolidarity (M2) retains 70% same-tenant cache reuse at +174.1% overhead — a better Pareto point than M1, but requires kernel-level changes to vLLM's BlockManager. Our novel M3 mitigation achieves the same oracle destruction (SR ≈ 0.0005) at only +178.0% overhead — 71.3% lower than M1 — by using Presidio NER to selectively isolate only PII-bearing requests without modifying the serving framework.
